A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mnemis research. Their text, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across pagination and table-number changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original Mnemis evaluations on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S, retrieval and backend-model ablations, and computational costs.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a human evaluation of 60 LoCoMo answers to check the LLM judge.

M1.justification: The dual-route framework and appendix prompts are retained. v2 expands documentation of speaker extraction and early stopping; v1 Appendix D already contains Speaker categorization and get_all_children instructions. These additions do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S with the same task coverage. The new human audit samples existing LoCoMo answers without introducing another dataset, population or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main experiments and appendix comparisons. v1 Tables 7–8 correspond to v2 Tables 8–9; added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a human-audit protocol: manually select three LLM-judged correct and three incorrect answers per LoCoMo user, totaling 60 of 1,540 instances, and apply LoCoMo grading criteria. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a limited analysis of LLM-judge reliability through comparison with human grading. Existing retrieval-route, top-k and backend-model ablations and the illustrative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new human audit reports agreement without adding uncertainty estimates or a statistical testing procedure.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports no human–LLM grading disagreements among the 60 sampled answers. Existing numerical results remain unchanged, including GPT-4.1-mini scores of 93.9 on LoCoMo at k=30 and 91.6 on LongMemEval-S.

T1.justification: The hierarchy constraints and other mathematical content are unchanged. v2 adds no formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same dual-route memory proposal and benchmark-performance claims. The human audit supplies additional support without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: Sections 2.2–2.3 newly explain how the Speaker branch provides alternative retrieval paths and reduces sensitivity to categorization errors, and how early stopping avoids unnecessary inference. Existing temporal-query and hierarchy-update limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents forced speaker extraction and early stopping more explicitly, and clarifies that Table 3 costs cover the entire dataset. New Table 7 identifies the human-audit samples, while the text states that detailed judgments are available in the project repository.

R1.justification: Seven cited works are added in the introduction and Related Work, including ModelGPT and Sigma. The substantive comparison with GraphRAG and Mnemis's novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds short Practical Scalability passages, Appendix B.1 and corresponding-author contact information, alongside limited wording edits. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the human-sample ID table and clarifies Table 3's caption. Existing appendix Tables 7–9 become Tables 8–10 with layout shifts; the five figures and existing table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The new human audit provides limited evidence supporting the LLM judge, with sample IDs enabling scrutiny. Clearer implementation explanations and whole-dataset cost reporting also improve transparency. The audit's small, manually selected sample limits the gain; the principal experiments and claims remain unchanged.
